symbols.summary: The words readers actually reached, in reading order.

groups.title: Progress
groups.summary: Where in a page reading stops.

symbols.name: ReadingStep
symbols.summary: One part as a point on its parent's sequence.

symbols.name: ReadingStop
symbols.summary: Two parts of one run, and the readers who reached the first and not the second.

symbols.name: ReadingRun
symbols.summary: One parent's children, in the order a reader meets them.

symbols.name: ReadingProgress
symbols.signature:
type ReadingProgress = {
    readonly treeId: TreeId;
    readonly revision: number;
    /**
     * The audience the reading was of, carried through unchanged.
     *
     * Carried rather than derived, and carried for one reason: an order over a
     * deployment's pages picks each page's door row by this trio and refuses to
     * count a page twice by it (`readingKeyOf`), and a progress reading that
     * dropped the audience would hand that order two forms of one page it could
     * not tell apart.
     */
    readonly audienceId: AudienceId | null;
    /**
     * Every audience the window named, carried through unchanged.
     *
     * Carried for the reason {@link ReadingProgress.audienceId} is, one step
     * further on: the pair of fields is what `audienceScopeRead` needs, and
     * without the census every reading downstream of this one gets `one` where
     * the window was two forms read as neither. More than one member with
     * {@link ReadingProgress.audienceId} `null` is that refusal, and what it
     * costs to drop is written on {@link ReadingProgress.views}.
     */
    readonly audiences: readonly AudienceId[];
    /**
     * The page's view floor, carried through from the reading unchanged.
     *
     * Zero means nothing stopped anywhere, so `runs` is empty rather than a page
     * of parts that all look skipped.
     *
     * **It does not mean nothing was measured, and that is the second job it was
     * doing.** A window holding two forms of the page with none asked for is read
     * as neither, so every part is `unknown` and this is nought while the
     * counters behind it are full and the door beside it has arrivals in it, which
     * is the page reading's refusal held against the door's sum. The
     * two states are told apart by the census above and nowhere else, which is
     * why it travels.
     */
    readonly views: number;
    /**
     * Every run of two or more children, in reading order.
     *
     * A run of one is left out: a stop is between two parts, and an only child has
     * nowhere for reading to stop. Every part of the page is a step in at most one
     * run — its parent's — so no reader's progress is counted at two depths.
     */
    readonly runs: readonly ReadingRun[];
    /**
     * The sharpest fall on the page: most views lost, then largest share, then
     * first in reading order.
     *
     * By views lost rather than by share, because *where does this page lose
     * readers* is a question about readers. A band two readers out of three
     * abandoned is a worse rate and a smaller problem than one four hundred out of
     * a thousand did, and ranking by share would put the former at the top of
     * every screen for ever.
     */
    readonly steepest: ReadingStop | null;
    /**
     * Parts that could not anchor a stop, because they reported something other
     * than coming into view.
     *
     * Empty on an ordinary page. A long list is a diagnosis: presses are being
     * delegated to regions that no `viewed` names, which is a sender or a
     * primitive not reporting what it is, rather than a page nobody read.
     */
    readonly unanchored: readonly NodeId[];
    /** Every run's {@link ReadingRun.gained}, added. */
    readonly gained: number;
};

symbols.name: readingProgressOf
symbols.summary: Where reading stops, from a reading of one revision.

groups.title: Ratios
groups.summary: A quotient of one window's figure against the other's, and the reason there is not one.

symbols.name: RatioAbsence
symbols.signature:
type RatioAbsence = 
/**
 * One of the two windows did not measure this, so there is nothing to divide.
 *
 * The absence is the other side's as much as this one's: a part that was a
 * leaf and now bears an inside has a share now and never had one, and a
 * window with no page views has no figure of any kind. What each side
 * withholds and why is that reading's own rule, and this says only that one
 * of them did.
 */
"unmeasured"
/**
 * Both windows measured it and the earlier one measured nought.
 *
 * A division by nought and not an absence of measurement, so the pair of
 * sides a comparison publishes beside this is worth reading: the later side
 * says whether the figure rose from nothing or stayed there, and the
 * movement of the two standings says it in words. *Nobody acted in this band
 * and four in ten do now* is this member with a later side above nought, and
 * it is the state a surface most wants to draw and could least afford to
 * read as *nothing to compare*.
 */
 | "from-nothing";
symbols.summary: Why there is no quotient.

symbols.name: RATIO_ABSENCES
symbols.summary: The closed set, for a surface accounting for every absent quotient.

symbols.name: describeRatioAbsence
symbols.summary: One line per absence, for a surface saying why a ratio is not there.

symbols.name: Ratio
symbols.summary: A quotient of the later window's figure by the earlier one's, or the reason there is none.

symbols.name: ratioOf
symbols.signature: const ratioOf: (was: number | null | undefined, now: number | null | undefined) => Ratio
symbols.summary: The later window's figure over the earlier one's, with the absence named.

groups.title: Reach
groups.summary: How far into a page readers get, as a share of the readers there were.

symbols.name: ReachSilence
symbols.signature:
type ReachSilence = 
/**
 * No page-view row for this tree and revision.
 *
 * Either the counter has never been written for it — a deployment whose
 * intake predates the column, or one whose rows have expired — or the caller
 * read the rows for something else. The counters are still a floor on how
 * many readers there were, which is what a reading reported before this
 * join existed, so a surface has something to fall back to and should say
 * which it is showing.
 */
"unmeasured"
/**
 * The row is there and nothing in it says a page view ever began.
 *
 * Two deployments look like this and the second is the one worth catching.
 * If no rollup has counted an appearance either, nobody has read this
 * revision and there is nothing to divide. If appearances have been counted,
 * **the senders are not marking their openings** — a page running a
 * broadcaster from before the marker shipped, or one whose opening delivery
 * is being lost — and every rate on the screen has no denominator while the
 * counters look healthy. That is a diagnosis nothing else in this subsystem
 * offers.
 */
 | "unopened"
/**
 * Readers arrived and no rollup has folded a window yet.
 *
 * Everything is `pending`. It is what the first minutes of a deployment look
 * like, and what a stalled collection looks like for ever, and the two are
 * told apart by whether the number moves.
 */
 | "uncounted";
symbols.summary: Why a share of readers cannot be given at all.

symbols.name: describeReachSilence
symbols.summary: One line per silence, for a surface putting the reading in front of a person.

symbols.name: PartReach
symbols.signature:
type PartReach = {
    readonly nodeId: NodeId;
    readonly type: PrimitiveType;
    /** What part it plays, or `null` where its type declared none. */
    readonly role: PrimitiveRole | null;
    /** 0 at the root, as the reading's outline gives it. */
    readonly depth: number;
    readonly standing: PartStanding;
    /**
     * Distinct page views that saw it, exactly as stored: added across rollup
     * windows and therefore generous.
     *
     * Published beside the shares rather than hidden behind them, because it is
     * the only figure here that is not a division and the one to fall back to
     * when the pair cannot be reconciled.
     */
    readonly reached: number;
    /**
     * The share of page views that got this far, as the rollups counted both
     * ends: `reached ÷ appearances`.
     *
     * The straddle over-count is in the numerator and the denominator and very
     * nearly divides out, which is what makes this the figure to show. It is an
     * estimate and not a bound, and the direction it leans is worth knowing: a
     * reader who stayed long enough to span two windows is counted twice on both
     * sides, and a reader who stays longer is likelier to have got deep into the
     * page — so for a part near the bottom this reads a little generous.
     *
     * **Its denominator is the page views that have been counted, which is not
     * every reader who arrived.** While openings are pending the two are
     * different populations, so this can sit above
     * {@link PartReach.atMost} — that is not a contradiction and the pending
     * figure is the explanation.
     *
     * `null` under a silence.
     */
    readonly share: number | null;
    /**
     * The most the share could be: `reached ÷ opened`, never above 1.
     *
     * A ceiling rather than an estimate. The openings are a count of readers that
     * no window boundary can inflate, and `reached` is at least the number of
     * readers who really got here, so the true share is at or below this.
     *
     * **For a part nearly everybody reaches it is 1 and says nothing**, and that
     * is the ordinary state rather than a fault: a root is in the viewport of
     * every page view, so where any visit spanned two windows its `reached` is
     * above the openings on its own. The estimate is the figure with information
     * in it there; this is the one that bounds a part further down.
     *
     * `null` under a silence.
     */
    readonly atMost: number | null;
    /**
     * The share applied to the exact count of readers who arrived — the number a
     * sentence can say out loud.
     *
     * Deliberately not rounded: it is a magnitude and not a census, and a surface
     * that rounds it is saying how precise it thinks it is.
     *
     * **One division of two whole numbers, not the share multiplied back up.**
     * The two are the same arithmetic in exact numbers and not in a float —
     * seven readers out of a hundred, times a hundred, is seven and a
     * quadrillionth, which is above the most readers who could have got there and
     * would make this figure break its own ceiling.
     *
     * Withheld in three states rather than given as a number nobody could stand
     * behind: under a silence; whenever the collection is behind, because
     * openings a rollup has not reached yet are readers whose reading nobody has
     * counted and projecting the folded rate onto them would answer a question
     * about people who were never measured; and where the two counters cannot be
     * reconciled, because a count of people above the number of people who
     * arrived is the one figure a screen must never show.
     */
    readonly readers: number | null;
    /**
     * The most readers who could have got here: the smaller of `reached` and the
     * openings, which is a whole number of real page views either way.
     *
     * `null` under a silence. Where {@link PartReach.readers} is given it is
     * never above this.
     */
    readonly atMostReaders: number | null;
    /**
     * More reach than there were page views to be reached in, so the share sits
     * above 1 and no figure here can be drawn.
     *
     * Reach is counted out of the same windows as the appearances it is divided
     * by, and a view that reached a part in a window is a view that appeared in
     * it — so rows written by the same rollups cannot produce this. Two things
     * can. **Node counters older than the page-view column**, added up over
     * windows whose appearances were never kept, which is what an upgraded
     * deployment's first reading looks like. Or a caller who concatenated two
     * reads of the counters instead of letting the store add them, which the
     * reading upstream reports as a duplicated node.
     *
     * It is not the ordinary straddle: `reached` above the *openings* is
     * expected, and is what {@link PartReach.atMost} being 1 means.
     *
     * A surface should show `reached` and say it cannot yet be put as a share.
     */
    readonly unreconciled: boolean;
};
symbols.summary: How far one part of a page got, against the readers there were.

symbols.name: PageReach
symbols.summary: A window of counters, read against the exact number of readers that window had.

symbols.name: pageReachOf
symbols.signature: const pageReachOf: (reading: PageReading, rows: readonly StoredPageViews[]) => PageReach
symbols.summary: Read a window's counters against the readers that window had.

groups.title: Readable
groups.summary: What *on screen* means, as the two numbers that decide it.

symbols.name: READABLE_VISIBLE_FRACTION
symbols.summary: At least this much of the element is visible.

symbols.name: READABLE_VIEWPORT_FRACTION
symbols.summary: Or the element fills at least this much of the window.

groups.title: Readership
groups.summary: Whether two windows of a page were read by the same readership.

symbols.name: READERSHIP_SHIFTED_ABOVE
symbols.summary: How much of a readership has to move before a comparison of two windows is not comparing like with like.

symbols.name: RegionMovement
symbols.signature:
type RegionMovement = 
/** Named in both windows, and more views in the later one. */
"grew"
/** Named in both windows, and fewer views in the later one. */
 | "shrank"
/** Named in both windows, and exactly as many views. */
 | "steady"
/**
 * Unnamed in the earlier window and named in the later one.
 *
 * Either it had nobody or it had too few to name, and which is not said.
 */
 | "thickened"
/**
 * Named in the earlier window and unnamed in the later one.
 *
 * The same conflation the other way round, and the one worth being clear
 * about: this is **not** *the readers from this country stopped coming*. It
 * is *there are no longer enough of them to say*, which includes none of
 * them and includes nearly enough of them.
 */
 | "thinned";
symbols.summary: What happened to one region between the two windows.

symbols.name: describeRegionMovement
symbols.summary: One line per movement, for a surface putting the comparison in front of a person.

symbols.name: RegionSide
symbols.summary: What one window's map said about one region, where it said anything.

symbols.name: ComparedRegion
symbols.summary: One region, as the two windows' maps have it.

symbols.name: ReadershipComparability
symbols.signature:
type ReadershipComparability =
/**
 * The mix cannot have moved far enough to matter — `movedAtMost` is under the
 * line, so the withheld buckets cannot carry it over.
 */
"like-for-like"
/** The mix moved, and the region that moved most is a place. */
 | "shifted"
/**
 * The mix moved, and the region that moved most is the bucket that names
 * nowhere.
 *
 * Worth its own member because it is almost never a fact about readers. The
 * unplaced bucket is what the platform in front of the application did not
 * say, so a swing in it is a proxy changed, a header dropped or a CDN
 * rerouted — a change in the measurement rather than in the readership, and a
 * surface that called it an audience shift would send somebody looking for
 * the wrong thing.
 */
 | "unplaced"
/**
 * `moved` is under the line and `movedAtMost` is over it: the floor is
 * withholding enough that the question cannot be answered either way.
 *
 * The ordinary state of a quiet page, and a correct answer rather than a
 * fault. A deployment that wants it settled needs more readers, not a smaller
 * floor.
 */
 | "unsettled"
/** One of the two windows counted no page views at all, so there is no mix to compare. */
 | "unmeasured"
/**
 * The two maps were floored differently, so nothing was compared.
 *
 * A bucket named in one and withheld in the other would then be an artefact
 * of the two floors rather than a movement of readers, and every figure built
 * on it would inherit that. Read both sides at the same floor — the higher of
 * the two, since a floor is raise-only.
 */
 | "incomparable"
/**
 * The two maps are of two audiences, so nothing was compared.
 *
 * This reading exists to say whether the comparison beside it is of like with
 * like, and a pair of two populations is the one case where the answer is
 * known in advance and is *no*. Two forms of a page are served to two
 * sets of readers by construction, so every shift here would be the
 * difference between two audiences' geographies reported as a readership that
 * moved — and reported by the one reading a surface trusts to catch exactly
 * that.
 *
 * Refused only where both maps name an audience and the two differ; a pair
 * spanning the migration that added the column, or one built by
 * `regionReadingOf` over a whole window, names none and is compared with the
 * two names in {@link ReadershipChange.audiences}.
 */
 | "different-audiences";
symbols.summary: Whether the comparison beside this one is comparing like with like.

symbols.name: describeReadershipComparability
symbols.summary: One line per standing, for a surface putting the comparison in front of a person.

symbols.name: UnaccountedShares
symbols.summary: What the comparison could not account for, as a share of each window's views.

symbols.name: Arrivals
symbols.summary: How many page views began in each window, which is the weight and never a trend.

symbols.name: ReadershipChange
symbols.signature:
type ReadershipChange = {
    /**
     * The floor both maps were read at, or `undefined` where they differ and
     * nothing was compared.
     */
    readonly floor: number | undefined;
    readonly comparability: ReadershipComparability;
    /**
     * The audience each map was of, where it named one.
     *
     * As every comparison in this subsystem carries it, and for the same reason: a
     * `null` on either side is why a pair of two populations can be compared here
     * rather than refused, and a surface saying so needs the field to say it.
     */
    readonly audiences: ComparedAudiences;
    /**
     * The audiences each map's rows named, which is what each side was a sum
     * over.
     *
     * Beside {@link ReadershipChange.audiences} rather than instead of it,
     * because the two answer different questions and a surface needs both: that
     * one is the form each map is **of**, this one is the forms each map **added
     * up**. A map read whole over a deployment serving two audiences names no
     * form and has two members here, which is the ordinary case for a deployment
     * serving two forms of a page and the one this field exists for.
     * *Both of these maps are sums over two of the forms you serve* is a caption,
     * where the silence that was there before was indistinguishable from a window
     * that named nothing at all.
     *
     * **Nothing is refused on it**. A deployment's two forms are served to
     * two sets of readers, but the readers are people and a person who arrived
     * arrived once — so adding two forms' arrivals is one readership, unlike
     * adding two forms' node counters, which is one number about two pages
     *. Carried under a silence and under none, as every census here is.
     */
    readonly populations: ComparedPopulations;
    /**
     * Half the sum of the absolute share movements over the regions both maps
     * name, in `[0, 1]`, or `undefined` where nothing was compared.
     *
     * A floor on how much the readership moved. The share of readers who would
     * have to be somewhere else for the two windows to have the same mix.
     */
    readonly moved: number | undefined;
    /**
     * {@link moved} plus the whole unaccounted share of both windows, capped at
     * 1, or `undefined` with it.
     *
     * A ceiling, and the two numbers together are the only honest statement this
     * can make on a page whose buckets are mostly under the floor.
     */
    readonly movedAtMost: number | undefined;
    /**
     * Every region either map names, most-moved first.
     *
     * Ranked by views moved rather than by share moved, which is the ranking rule
     * this subsystem uses everywhere: a country of forty readers that
     * halved is a smaller fact than one of four hundred that moved a tenth. A
     * `thinned` or `thickened` row is ranked by the one figure it has, which
     * treats the withheld side as nought and therefore ranks such a row as high
     * as it could possibly deserve.
     */
    readonly regions: readonly ComparedRegion[];
    /**
     * The region carrying the largest absolute {@link ComparedRegion.shift}, or
     * `undefined` where no region is named in both maps.
     *
     * What `shifted` and `unplaced` are told apart by, and the first thing a
     * person reading a shifted comparison wants.
     */
    readonly loudest: ReaderRegion | undefined;
    /**
     * The share of each window's views that is in no comparable row: its withheld
     * buckets, and the buckets the other window withheld.
     *
     * The width of the bound on {@link moved}, and a measurement in its own
     * right — a deployment reading two thirds of its arrivals as unaccounted is
     * being told that its traffic is spread thinner than its floor, which no
     * single window's map says.
     */
    readonly unaccounted: UnaccountedShares;
    /**
     * Page views that began in each window, named and withheld.
     *

symbols.signature:
type RegionReadingFor = {
    /** The revision's own map, floored. */
    readonly reading: RegionReading;
    /**
     * Rows for another tree or another revision, and ignored.
     *
     * Counting another revision's arrivals into this one's map is the mistake
     * that would make a readership comparison compare a revision with itself.
     */
    readonly foreign: number;
    /**
     * Rows for this revision in another audience, and ignored.
     *
     * A page served in two forms counts each form's arrivals on its own row
     *, and both forms' readers are real readers of the page — so this is
     * neither foreign nor a doubled bucket. It is the other form's readership,
     * which is a different map and not part of this one: a mix taken over both
     * is one composition of two populations, and a comparison beside it would be
     * comparing neither form with itself.
     */
    readonly otherAudience: number;
    /**
     * Rows naming a region **and an audience** this revision already had a row
     * for, beyond the first, every one of which was ignored.
     *
     * A store keeps one row per tree, revision, audience and region, so this
     * cannot come out of one read — it happens when a caller concatenates two
     * windows of rows, and the store's counts are already running totals rather
     * than a window's. Adding them would double a bucket, which is the one error
     * in this subsystem that cannot be undone afterwards, so the first row
     * stands and the fact is reported.
     *
     * **The audience is part of what makes two rows two rows**, and leaving it
     * out was a quiet undercount. A revision served in two forms
     * has two rows for one country, one per form, and a map read whole of such a
     * revision dropped the second as the first handed in twice: 60 views
     * published where 460 arrived, with the loss reported as a count of
     * duplicates nobody would read as an undercount. A form's own map is
     * unaffected — the audience is picked before this, so region and audience key
     * the same rows region alone did.
     */
    readonly duplicated: number;
};

symbols.name: FunnelAnswer
Rollup
symbols.signature:
type Rollup = {
    readonly tallies: readonly ReaderTally[];
    readonly funnels: readonly FunnelAnswer[];
    /** Distinct page views seen, across every tree and revision in the input. */
    readonly views: number;
    /**
     * The same page views, per tree and revision — one appearance each, in this
     * window.
     *
     * Held apart from `views` because it is the number the durable page-view
     * counter keeps, and it is only worth keeping beside the exact count of page
     * views that *began*: the difference between the two is the straddle that
     * makes a distinct count added across windows generous, measured rather than
     * bounded. A revision whose batches carried no view key is absent
     * rather than nought — there is nothing to compare, and a zero row would read
     * as *no readers* rather than as *nobody minted a key*.
     */
    readonly appearances: readonly RevisionViews[];
    /**
     * Batches that carried no view key.
     *
     * Their occurrences are counted like any other; their views are not, because
     * there is no honest number to add. Treating each uncorrelated batch as its
     * own view would inflate every denominator by however often a page happened
     * to flush, which is a number about the network rather than about readers.
     * Reported so a portal can say the rate is computed over fewer views than the
     * totals, instead of showing a rate that is quietly wrong.
     */
    readonly uncorrelated: number;
    /**
     * Batches this fold refused as a repeat of one it had already folded.
     *
     * A sender may deliver the same batch twice — a host's retry queue draining
     * after an outage is the case `MAX_BATCHES_PER_DELIVERY` exists to allow, and
     * an edge network replaying a `POST` is the case nobody writes. What that
     * costs is **asymmetric and therefore invisible**: `views`, `reached`,
     * `engaged` and `appearances` are sets of view keys, so a repeat adds the key
     * it already holds and moves nothing, while `dwellMs`, `activations`, `opens`,
     * `closes` and `completions` are occurrences and double. Every rate this
     * subsystem publishes divides the second kind by the first, so a repeat does
     * not look like noise — it looks like a reader who was twice as interested,
     * and the cost of it is permanent.
     *
     * So a batch identical to one already folded in this window is folded once and
     * counted here. **Only where it carries a view key**: without one, two
     * identical batches are as likely to be two readers in the same millisecond as
     * one batch arriving twice, and dropping a reader to avoid a repeat is the
     * worse of the two mistakes.
     *
     * Reported rather than silent, because the number is a fact about a
     * deployment's senders and not about its readers: a window with repeats in it
     * every run is a retry loop somebody should find.
     */
    readonly redelivered: number;
};

type SilenceSubject = 
/** One revision of one page, and the window of counters read against it. */
"page"
/** One part of one revision. */

/**
 * The two readings held against each other, naming neither side.
 *
 * The distinction that makes this worth having: *one of the two windows held
 * no page views* does not say which, so a card cannot draw it over the page
 * somebody is looking at. A reading of one page that says the same thing is
 * about the page on the screen.
 */
 | "comparison"
/**
 * One kind of part, everywhere it stands in the pages read.
 *
 * The fourth subject, and the first that is not a thing a deployment holds. A
 * page, a part and a pair all exist because something was read; a kind comes

symbols.name: SilenceCondition
symbols.signature:
type SilenceCondition =
/** The two readings are of different trees, so nothing in either is comparable. */
"two-pages"
/**
 * The two readings are of two audiences, so they are of two populations.
 *
 * The sibling of `two-pages`, and the pair is why this is its own condition.
 * Two pages make every figure absurd; two forms of one page compare cleanly
 * and carry a sentence about a readership that was varied rather than held
 * still. Reported only where both readings name an audience and the two
 * differ.
 */
 | "two-audiences"
/**
 * Nothing reported a view of it.
 *
 * Of a page, the window's counters say no view of this revision happened. Of
 * a part, no view reported that part coming into view, which a window with
 * readers in it can say about any part they did not reach.
 */
 | "no-view-reported"
/**
 * There is no page-view row at the door for this revision.
 *
 * Not the same state as nothing having been seen, and the pair is the reason
 * this mapping is published. The node counters can hold a window of readers
 * while this row is missing — a deployment whose intake predates the column,
 * one whose rows have expired, or a caller that fetched the rows for
 * something else — and the counters are then still a floor on how many
 * readers there were.
 */
 | "no-arrivals-counted"
/**
 * The row is there and nothing in it says a page view ever began.
 *
 * Two deployments look like this, and which one it is turns on whether any
 * appearance has been counted: nobody has read this revision, or **the
 * senders are not marking their openings** and every rate on the screen has
 * no denominator while the counters look healthy. The reading publishes both
 * numbers, so the diagnosis is a subtraction a surface can make; the
 * condition is what the two have in common and no more.
 */
 | "no-openings-marked"
/** Readers arrived and no rollup has folded a window of their reading yet. */
 | "no-window-folded"
/** It says nothing that could have been read: no words, and nothing undeclared either. */
 | "says-nothing"
/**
 * Some of its words are a floor, because a type in it declares no `copy`
 *.
 *
 * A count of words survives this and a mean of them does not, which is why
 * the readings that hit it withhold a figure rather than a row.
 */
 | "words-a-floor"
/**
 * It reports more readers than it has views, which no rollup produces.
 *
 * A reading assembled by hand, or by a sender that is not one. It is the
 * alarm a reading raises where a figure would otherwise stay plausible while
 * being about nothing.
 */
 | "readers-above-views"
/** The change left no word of the page as it was, so there is no carried text to read. */
 | "nothing-carried"
/**
 * The window holds actions and credits none of them to a reader.
 *
 * A press is filed against the control and credited to the addressed ancestors
 * the signal carries, so a sender whose delegated signals have no
 * `within` adds occurrences and no reader anywhere. The counters are present
 * and look healthy; what is wrong is that every share built on them is a
 * nought that is a filing rule rather than a measurement.
 *
 * The one condition here about a **nought that is not an absence**, which is
 * why no earlier set could report it. The occurrence counts survive it intact,
 * because they are filed against the part a reader used and need no ancestry.
 */
 | "no-action-credited"
/**
 * There is none of it in the pages read.
 *
 * Not a measurement that is missing: the thing being asked about is absent
 * from the library, which only a reading keyed by a vocabulary can say. A role
 * no primitive declares and a type nothing places are both this, and the
 * instruction it carries is the opposite of every other condition here —
 * there is nothing to measure rather than nothing measured.
 */
 | "nothing-of-the-kind"
/**
 * It has nothing inside it, so there is nothing a reader could act in.
 *
 * A press is filed against the control and credited to the addressed
 * ancestors it happened inside, so a part with no element part under it
 * reports a nought for ever — which is the state `says-nothing` is for a
 * page's words, one counter across.
 *
 * **The second condition here about the shape of the page rather than about
 * the window**, and the pair is what makes the claim above still hold: these
 * are states of the world, and the way a new one arrives is with a reading
 * that can be in one nothing before it could. A reading of what readers *did*
 * to a **kind** of part is the first that can report it, because a kind is
 * answered over the places it stands and the question does not exist where
 * none of them has an inside.
 */
 | "nothing-inside"
/**
 * Its counters are there and not one of them reports being reached.
 *
 * Readers arrived — the window holds page views — and every part of what the
 * figure is about has a row whose reach is nought. A part that reported
 * something other than coming into view is `unknown` and never `skipped`
 *, because a reader who pressed something inside a band no `viewed`
 * ever named plainly had it in front of them, and a mean taken over nought
 * reader-words would print *nobody read any of this* as a measurement.
 *
 * **The sibling of `no-action-credited`, and the pair is the reason this is
 * its own condition rather than a second spelling of `no-view-reported`.**
 * That is a nought which is a filing rule, this is a nought which is a
 * missing report, and `no-view-reported` is a nought which is a reader who
 * was not there. A deployment handed the wrong one of the three looks in the
 * wrong place: at its funnel pairs, at its senders, or at nothing, because
 * quiet traffic is not a fault.
 */
 | "no-reach-reported"
…

     * any of them: every call is one delivery's worth of arrivals, so a store

     * `aud_everyone`, so a door that serves one form of every page calls this
     * exactly as it did.
     *

symbols.name: AudienceCounters

symbols.name: ReaderTallyStore
symbols.signature:
interface ReaderTallyStore extends ReaderOpeningCounter {
    /**
     * Add a whole window's counters to what is already there, every audience in
     * it, in one atomic write — creating rows that do not exist yet.
     *
     * **This is the method a collection run calls, and the atomicity is the
     * reason it exists rather than a property it happens to have.**
     *
     * A window holds whatever arrived in it, so a deployment serving two forms of
     * a page holds two audiences interleaved and is folded once per audience
     *. Writing those folds as separate calls leaves a state between them
     * where some are durable and the rest are not — and because counting and
     * forgetting are one operation (`collect.ts`), the buffer still holds the
     * window, so the next run folds it again and **adds the already-durable
     * audiences a second time.** Of a tally's nine counters, `views`, `reached`
     * and `engaged` are distinct counts and would move little; `dwellMs`,
     * `activations`, `opens`, `closes` and `completions` are occurrences and
     * would double, which every rate in this subsystem divides by the first kind
     * — so the damage is invisible, permanent and looks like a readership
     * twice as interested as it was.
     *
     * So the window is one write or it is none. A store that cannot be atomic
     * over several audiences cannot be correct here, which is why this is a
     * required method rather than a capability a caller probes for.
     *
     * Two entries naming one audience are added together, not refused: the
     * guarantee is the same one `counters.ts` gives for two rows naming one
     * counter, and it is here so that the two shipped stores cannot disagree
     * about it.
     */
    readonly applyWindow: (window: readonly AudienceCounters[], at: string) => Promise<Result<void, ReaderSignalStoreError>>;
    /**
     * One audience's counters, which is {@link applyWindow} over a single entry
     * and is implemented as exactly that in both shipped stores — so the two
     * cannot drift on the half that matters.
     *
     * Kept because a caller composing counters by hand — a backfill, a fixture, a
     * migration — has one audience and no window, and should not have to wrap it
     * in a list to say so.
     */
    readonly apply: (counters: AppliedCounters, at: string,
    /**
     * The audience whose counters these are. Omitted is `aud_everyone`.
     */
    audience?: AudienceId) => Promise<Result<void, ReaderSignalStoreError>>;
    readonly tallies: (request?: TallyReadRequest) => Promise<Result<readonly StoredTally[], ReaderSignalStoreError>>;
    readonly funnels: (request?: TallyReadRequest) => Promise<Result<readonly StoredFunnel[], ReaderSignalStoreError>>;
    /**
     * How many page views there were, which is the denominator every rate on a
     * screen needs and the only row here written from two sides.
     */
    readonly pageViews: (request?: TallyReadRequest) => Promise<Result<readonly StoredPageViews[], ReaderSignalStoreError>>;
}

     * the floor bites harder the narrower the group** — the same sentence
     * `regionReadingFor` carries. Thirty views of one country split twelve and
     * eighteen across two forms are a readership the whole map names and both
     * form maps withhold. A rung that published only the split would answer
     * *where are my readers* worse than the two calls it replaces.
     *
     * Summing two forms' arrivals is right here and wrong on the counters, and
     * the asymmetry is a published one: a person who arrived arrived once,
     * whichever form they were served, while adding two forms' node counters is
     * one number about two pages.
     */
    readonly readership: RegionReading;
    /**
     * Rows beyond the first for one tree, revision, form and region — dropped
     * from every map, and counted here.
     *
     * A store keeps one row per that key, so this cannot come out of one read: it
     * is a caller concatenating two windows whose counts are already running
     * totals. Adding them would double a bucket, which is the one error here that
     * cannot be undone afterwards, so the first row stands and the fact is
     * a number. The same rule `regionReadingFor` applies to one revision, applied
     * once to the whole window so the maps and the readership drop the same rows.
     */
    readonly duplicated: number;
};

groups.title: Calibration
groups.summary: Confidence is self-graded and trusted on purpose, on one condition: that it be calibrated. This is the measurement half of that promise. It compares what the model claimed against what became of the claim, and it changes nothing — no threshold moves, no policy reads it.

symbols.name: UNJUDGED_REASONS
symbols.summary: The buckets a fold has to open before the first proposal arrives, so a reason nobody hit still reads as zero rather than as missing.

symbols.name: verdictOf
symbols.summary: A repair is scored as its own proposal, not merged into the one it replaced. Both graded themselves, and the refusal that prompted the repair is exactly the case where the grade was wrong — averaging it away would hide the datapoint calibration exists to collect.

symbols.name: CalibrationScore
ConfidenceBucket
symbols.summary: Half-open `[lower, upper)`, except the last bucket, which is closed so 1 has a home.

symbols.name: PolicyCalibration
symbols.signature:
type PolicyCalibration = {
    /**
     * Which policy judged these claims, as its own dispositions named it.
     *
     * `null` means this window never saw the judgment — the page opened after the
     * disposition and before the commit, say. Distinct from the recorded string
     * `UNATTRIBUTED_POLICY_ID`, which is a judgment that really was made before the
     * Gate wrote down which policy made it. One is a gap in the reader, the other
     * is a gap in the record, and merging them would let a fixed record look like a
     * short page.
     */
    readonly policyId: string | null;
    readonly overall: CalibrationScore;
    readonly buckets: readonly ConfidenceBucket[];
    /**
     * The distinct fingerprints the judgments in this segment named, sorted.
     *
     * A name is host-declared, and hosts are asked to rename a policy they edit.
     * More than one fingerprint under one name means that did not happen, and this
     * row is pooling gates that differ by more than what they are called — the same
     * error the segments exist to correct, one level down. `rulesetContinuityOf`
     * reads this list; the list itself is carried so a host can match a digest to
     * the configuration it is looking at.
     */
    readonly fingerprints: readonly string[];
    /**
     * Judged claims in this segment whose disposition named no fingerprint. Kept
     * beside the list rather than folded into it: one fingerprint plus twelve
     * unfingerprinted judgments is not a segment shown to be constant, and a list
     * of length one would say it was.
     */
    readonly unfingerprinted: number;
    /**
     * The distinct sets of optional write-path checks the judgments in this
     * segment were made under, each in canonical order.
     *
     * The fingerprint above proves which *rules* judged these claims and cannot
     * reach the two seams a composition root hands over separately, either of
     * which can turn an `accepted` into a `rejected`. So a segment
     * whose `fingerprints` has one member is a segment that was judged under one
     * set of rules, and this is the rest of the sentence: whether it was judged by
     * one write path. More than one member here and a survival rate that moved is
     * explained by the wiring rather than by the model.
     *
     * Sets rather than a verdict, for the reason `fingerprints` is a list rather
     * than a `RulesetContinuity`: `checksContinuityOf` reads this, and the lists
     * themselves are what a host matches against its own composition root.
     */
    readonly checkSets: readonly (readonly WriteCheck[])[];
    /**
     * Judged claims in this segment whose disposition named no check list. Kept
     * beside the sets for the reason `unfingerprinted` is kept beside the
     * fingerprints: one set plus twelve judgments that recorded none is not a
     * segment shown to have been judged by one write path.
     */
    readonly unrecordedChecks: number;
};
symbols.summary: A calibration reading confined to the claims one policy judged.
